sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Eochaid, spelled also Echid or Eochaidh, is an Irish hero. The name means horseman. Irish myth gives the name to countless kings and heroes. They may all stem from a single ancient figure. Some were gods, while other men may have been drawn into the worship of a sun god. The chief bearers of the name are treated in their own entries. Each ruled or fought in his own corner of the legend. The name recurs so often that scholars read it as a badge of an old continental deity.
